### English source — DO NOT EDIT

<!-- SOURCE_TURN_001_BEGIN -->
As an educator in the field of design thinking, I am constantly looking for ways to improve my courses and help my students achieve their fullest potential. In recent years, I have made a significant development to my design thinking course that has yielded outstanding results.

The development that I made to my design thinking course involves incorporating more hands-on, project-based learning activities into the curriculum. I recognized that while traditional lecture-based teaching methods have their place in education, students in design thinking courses often learn best through experience and experimentation.

To achieve this, I added more design challenges, design sprints, and real-world case studies to the course curriculum. I also made sure that each activity was structured in a way that allowed students to work collaboratively and learn from one another. By doing so, my students gained practical experience in applying design thinking principles to real-world problems, which significantly enhanced their understanding of the subject matter.

One particular example of the impact of this development occurred during a project-based learning activity where students were tasked with designing a new product for a local business. The activity required students to utilize the design thinking process from start to finish, including conducting user research, creating personas, and prototyping their product. Through this exercise, my students gained valuable experience in applying design thinking principles to real-world problems.

As a result of this development, I have observed significant improvements in my students' understanding of design thinking concepts, as well as their ability to apply these principles to real-world scenarios. Moreover, student feedback has been overwhelmingly positive, with many reporting that the hands-on, project-based learning approach helped them develop practical skills that they can apply in their careers.

Overall, the development that I made to my design thinking course has been highly successful in enhancing my students' learning experience. By incorporating more hands-on, project-based learning activities, I have helped my students gain practical experience in applying design thinking principles to real-world problems, setting them up for success in their future careers.
<!-- SOURCE_TURN_001_END -->
